heading: Profiles, paths and which value wins
body: When the Yon server starts, YON_PROFILE selects server/application-<profile>.json. Objects merge recursively (at every level of nesting). An array in the profile replaces the base array. Tachyon does not join the two arrays. For the server host and port, the source with the highest priority wins. From highest to lowest, the sources are: CLI --host and --port flags that you pass, the profile file, the base server/application.json, and the command defaults. So a flag that you pass overrides yon.server.host and yon.server.port. Values from the parent application environment no longer override configuration or provide secrets. .env names map to paths by underscores. They are not interpolated (Tachyon does not replace references inside them). A .env name may replace a single value of the JSON configuration: that value declares the type. If the JSON value is true or false, the .env value must be exactly true or false. If it is a whole number, the .env value must be a whole number. If it is any other number, the .env value must be a number. Otherwise the value stays a string. A value that does not fit stops ty start with TY2010, which names the .env name and the expected type but never the value. A .env name cannot replace a list or an object. A .env file that sets a name Tachyon keeps for its own transport, profile, endpoint, runtime or isolation policy is refused: YON_PROFILE, YON_HOST, YON_HOSTNAME, YON_PORT, YON_ISOLATION, YON_SKIP_BUNDLE, YON_APPLICATION_JSON, YON_RESOURCE_ENDPOINT, YON_RESOURCE_TOKEN, YON_HANDLER_PROTOCOL, YON_JAVASCRIPT_RUNTIME, YON_PYTHON_RUNTIME, YON_RUBY_RUNTIME, YON_SERVER, and every name that starts with YON_SERVER_ or YON_FIRECRACKER_. Empty path segments, duplicate names, and a name that is both a scalar (a single value) and an object fail. Their errors are redacted, which means they hide the values. To expose the server beyond the local machine (non-loopback), you still need --allow-non-loopback. In production, a secret manager may mount the .env file. Tac builds read only the tac member of client/manifest.json. No profile is merged over it.
